units: <cite ref="Tosefta Chullin 8:16">Tosef. Ḥull. VIII, 16</cite> <he>ל׳ עובר וכ׳</he> if a Roman legion passes from quarters to quarters, whatever has been used as a cover or shelter, (v. <cite ref="A00500"><he>אָהַל</he></cite>) is unclean; <cite ref="Chullin 123a:3">Ḥull. 123ᵃ</cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 4:6">Gen. R. s. 4</cite>, end <he>ל׳ קשה</he> an intractable legion. Tanḥ. Vayesheb 3 <he>ל׳ אחד נאה ומשובח ראשן וכ׳</he> (not <he>ראשו</he>) a legion of fine and distinguished men, their heads reaching up to the capital of pillars; a. fr.—Pl. <he>לִגְיוֹנִין</he>, <he>לִגְיוֹנִים</he>, <he>לִגְיוֹנוֹת</he>, <cite ref="L00031"><he>לִי׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 4:6">Ib.</cite> <he>ל׳ אלו אינן וכ׳</he> these legions are not worth anything (in the economy of Providence).
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 1:2">Num. R. s. 1</cite> <he>אין שבח … שימנה לגיונו עם הל׳</he> it is not worthy of the King that his own legion (body-guard) be counted with the legions.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:1:14">Y. Taan. II, 65ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>שני ל׳ קשים</he> two wild-tempered legions.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15:13">Ex. R. s. 15</cite> <he>דוכוס שזרקו לו הל׳ פורפירא</he> a general before whom the legions cast the purple cloak (whom they proclaim emperor).
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15:8">Ib.</cite> <he>ומוציא הלגיונין וכ׳</he> and leads the legions out (in parade), and this dates the beginning of his rule.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 16:1">Lev. R. s. 16</cite>, end <he>קורא הקב״ה ל׳ שלו</he> the Lord summons his legions (to execute punishment); a. e.
